legion-retro: the docs/solutions/ conventions the corrected note must keep (front matter schema, the 'Extends <path>.' first line) and the supersede rule the plan consciously does not take, with its stated reason.
dispatch-first: search Dispatch before posting any finding; the planner has already posted the /tmp correction on dispatch://INFRA-51, so do not post it again.
dispatch: the writing rules for any Dispatch comment or message this phase posts, and the 2,000-character limit.
test: legion-worker: the tester's charter — drive the real surface (a live role container), read CI for everything static, and write the test handoff with the implementer's proof judged.

findings.finding: F1 (blocker): the spec's premise is false for every role container, and the spec orders the note to assert it ('Say why /tmp is safe here in those words'). Evidence: docs/kubernetes.md:1189-1190 and :1703-1705; podkind.go:130-177 and names.go:89-92 (the memory tmp volume is workspace-fetch's alone); testdata/golden/root.json (no role container mounts /tmp); the two INFRA-43 notes.
findings.answer: The plan writes the measured cause instead: in a role container /tmp, $HOME and ~/.cache are one charged container filesystem, and the memory-backed /tmp belongs to workspace-fetch alone. Recorded as a spec departure below, named in the completion summary, and sent to the architect, which decides whether the spec changes.

findings.finding: F2 (blocker): under the spec's cause the note's TMPDIR bullet becomes unmotivated and a reader would conclude TMPDIR=/tmp is fine — the exact action the issue wants to prevent. No role container sets TMPDIR (manifest.go:728-736 sets it for workspace-fetch only), so every tool defaults to the charged /tmp.
findings.answer: Plan point 5 keeps the TMPDIR bullet and restates its reason from the corrected cause: apt-get download, dpkg-deb -x and the Playwright install stage through TMPDIR, which no role container sets, so they land on the charged /tmp unless TMPDIR is exported onto the issue volume.

findings.finding: F3 (high): '1Gi per container' is the admitted bound on this GKE deployment only and contradicts the 20Gi/10Gi limits docs/kubernetes.md:1167-1184 documents; the clamp (live_lifecycle_test.go:311-331, confirmed live 2026-10-17) is in no prose doc.
findings.answer: Plan point 4 has the note name the clamp and the deployment, cite live_lifecycle_test.go beside dispatch://INFRA-51, and say that on a cluster admitting the configured limit the number differs while the mechanism does not. Correcting docs/kubernetes.md's table is out of scope and reported to the architect.

findings.finding: F4 (high): edit in place (the spec's 'Rewrite that note') or write a successor with supersedes: (skill://legion-retro's rule for a wrongly-stated topic). The supersede route leaves the wrong cause unmarked in the file other documents link.
findings.answer: The plan edits in place, with the reason recorded in the plan and required in the pull-request body: the retro rule governs a retro's own durable output and exists against same-hour cross-tree edits, this is an implementing diff on the issue whose purpose is that file, and acceptance criterion 1 is about what a reader of that note meets. The plan also binds this issue's own retro to a separate learning rather than a third restatement. The architect may overrule.

findings.finding: F5 (high): the scope line holds only if the file keeps its path: docs/solutions/legion/a-capability-a-plan-declares-unavailable-is-a-claim-until-someone-tried-it-INFRA-44.md:52 links the note by path, and the note's own 'Extends ...' first line must survive.
findings.answer: The plan keeps the path, file name, title, H1 and the Extends line, so no other file is edited and that cross-reference keeps resolving.

findings.finding: F6 (high): acceptance criterion 2 ('a reader can tell which directories are charged') has no decidable check, and the spec's own list is partial (it omits Oh My Pi's state home and the /var/run/legion/* directories).
findings.answer: The plan enumerates the eleven paths the note must place on the charged / not-charged split, and makes the check one grep per path against the note, with a negative control (the note on main contains no /home/legion/.local/state).

findings.finding: F7 (high): acceptance criterion 3 names a link check that does not exist: docs.yaml's path filters exclude docs/solutions/**, its link validator covers docs/site only, and nothing else validates markdown links.
findings.answer: The plan restates the criterion as the Tests workflow's lint, typecheck and test jobs green at the head (run id recorded) plus an explicit hand check that every docs/solutions/... path the note cites exists at that head. Recorded as a spec departure; the architect may reword the criterion.

findings.finding: F8 (high): 'documentation only: no code, no test' does not exempt the pull request from the implementer's and tester's E2E proof lines, and the issue names no surface or command.
findings.answer: The plan names the surface (a live role container of an Agent Sandbox issue pod, plus the pod shape the daemon renders) and gives each criterion its command, observation and negative control, including a 200 MiB write under /tmp versus /legion measured with du -sx /.

findings.finding: F9 (high): the note is told to cite dispatch://INFRA-51, which is where the false sentence was posted and which feeds the in-progress fleet fix on dispatch://INFRA-31.
findings.answer: The planner posted the measurement back on dispatch://INFRA-51 as a reply to that read (comment 0ce1448c-ccbc-4b5f-aaaf-60dce4c5eb05). The note cites only the parts of that read that stand: the eviction events naming the implementer, the 1 GiB bound, and the 4.4 GiB of Go caches.

findings.finding: F10 (medium): docs/solutions/legion/a-port-held-in-an-issue-pod-...-LEGION-695.md:37 tells a role to build its Postgres harness under /tmp, which the measured cause makes wrong; the two INFRA-43 notes already agree with the measurement.
findings.answer: Out of this issue's one-file scope and reported to the architect as a candidate follow-up issue. The plan states that the two INFRA-43 notes are deliberately untouched, so a reviewer does not read their absence as an omission.

findings.finding: F11 (medium): the spec says nothing about the note's front matter.
findings.answer: The plan fixes it: keep date, status, module and the existing tags, add the eviction tag, and add INFRA-69 and this change's pull request to related_issues. Title, H1 and path do not change.

findings.finding: F12 (medium): 'keep the recipe and the evidence' draws no line, and the note's first bullet mixes the cause with a symptom description that stays true.
findings.answer: The plan names the boundary: the stated mechanism is rewritten, the symptom description (a kill with no disk message, the reset filesystem) is kept and re-reasoned, and the Extends line, the recipe sentences and the existing Evidence paragraph (the two green rounds, 299 passed) stay word for word, with the new measurements added below them.

findings.finding: F13 (medium): no repository source supports the claim that a large write to a memory-backed path 'spends memory rather than the storage budget'.
findings.answer: The claim is dropped: under the corrected cause there is no memory-backed /tmp in a role container, so the note never makes it. Where the note names the memory-backed tmp volume at all, it names it as workspace-fetch's and cites podkind.go.

specDepartures.spec: The spec's 'What was measured since' and 'What to change' state that /tmp is memory-backed on this deployment and instruct the note to say 'why /tmp is safe here in those words: it is memory-backed, not merely temporary, so a large write there spends memory rather than the storage budget'.
specDepartures.plan: The note says the opposite: a role container mounts no /tmp, so its /tmp, its $HOME and its ~/.cache are one container filesystem and all three are charged against the same per-container limit; the memory-backed tmp volume belongs to the workspace-fetch setup container alone. The note also names Oh My Pi's state home /home/legion/.local/state/<role> as charged, which the spec omits.
specDepartures.evidence: Measured 2026-10-20T22:20Z in the planner container of this issue's own pod: /proc/mounts has no /tmp line; stat -c '%d' gives device 83 for /tmp, /home/legion and /home/legion/.cache, 56 for /home/legion/.config, 97 for /var/run/legion/state, 87 for /legion; du -sx / is 42 MB. In the tree: podkind.go:130-177 and names.go:89-92 mount the memory tmp volume in workspace-fetch alone; testdata/golden/root.json shows no /tmp mount in any of the six role containers; docs/kubernetes.md:1189-1190 and :1703-1705 already state it.

summary: '/tmp is memory-backed, so neither counts toward that limit' becomes: only the issue volume /legion, the sessions directory and the in-memory /home/legion/.config and /var/run/legion/* directories are uncharged; /tmp is charged like the home directory.
'a large download under /tmp spends memory rather than the storage budget' is withdrawn for role containers.
acceptance: Acceptance line 1 ('the note's cause is the measured one') is met against the measurement above rather than against the spec's sentence about /tmp.

specDepartures.spec: Acceptance: 'the repository's own lint and link checks pass on it.'
specDepartures.plan: The plan proves the Tests workflow's lint, typecheck and test jobs green at the head and adds a hand check that every docs/solutions/... path the note cites exists there, because no link check covers docs/solutions/.
specDepartures.evidence: .github/workflows/docs.yaml's push and pull_request path filters are docs/site/**, packages/**, skills/**, scripts/third-party-notices.ts and two workflow/script paths — docs/solutions/** triggers nothing — and its starlight link validator runs over docs/site only. .github/workflows/pr-and-main.yaml runs lint, typecheck and test on every pull request with no path filter; in lint, only check-private-names.sh (which bans any *.ts.net host) can bite a markdown file, since check-plugin-names.sh excludes docs/solutions/ and Biome has no markdown rules.

acceptance: The 'link checks' clause names a check that does not exist for this path; the plan substitutes the named CI jobs plus an explicit path-resolution check.
